attribution_protocol.partition_basis: SHA-256(seed:language:canonical work_id), ranked within author and assigned round-robin to three whole-work partitions; legacy fixtures without work_id use language:author:display work
attribution_protocol.model: cosine nearest author centroid after training-only standardization
attribution_protocol.verification_calibration: threshold permits at most 5% negative calibration matches
attribution_protocol.rejection_calibration: threshold accepts at least 95% genuine known-author calibration matches
attribution_protocol.confidence: Conditional descriptive 95% intervals from whole-work resampling of fixed predictions; no refitting and no adjustment for shared training/candidate dependencies; zero/all-event rate boundaries guarded by work-level binomial limits
attribution_protocol.scope: reference-corpus lexical baseline; not historical scripture attribution or AI-profile validation

arb.reason: not selected or no acquired reference corpus; not a passing result

source_manifests.selection_protocol: Selected before scoring: choose three substantial, conventionally attributed distinct works per author, with at least 2,000 extracted Greek tokens each. Include three Attic forensic orators and two authors of Socratic prose for shared-genre/topic challenges. Lucian supplies a later author and a separate same-work edition control. No work, author, threshold, or feature is selected by observed benchmark accuracy.
source_manifests.attribution_caveat: Author identities are conventional Perseus catalog labels, not independent proof of ancient historical authorship. This is a small convenience benchmark of edited literary Greek, not scripture, and cannot validate biblical attribution, number of hands, or Hebrew/Arabic transfer. The same editor/edition tradition is often confounded with author; coarse genre/topic labels do not fully control subgenre, subject, chronology, or literary dependence. Forensic speeches may be ghostwritten for speakers; the author label refers to the attributed composer.

source_manifests.selection_protocol: Before inspecting classifier scores, choose four original prose works of 3000 to 30000 normalized tokens per author from four late nineteenth/early twentieth century Hebrew writers. Inspect catalogue entries and openings for shared modern social/psychological fiction. Exclude translated works, duplicate editions, biblical/historical retellings and folklore collections, or records with editorial prefaces whose voice cannot be separated confidently. Prefer earliest eligible catalogue IDs for Brenner, Gnessin and Bershadsky; for Berdyczewski choose four eligible modern stories after inspecting the first 65 prose records. Eligibility applies to the extracted body, not publisher text. This is a convenience sample, not a preregistered representative author sample.
source_manifests.attribution_caveat: Modern Hebrew is separated by centuries and substantial linguistic, literary, editorial and transmission differences from Biblical Hebrew. Results cannot establish scriptural authorship, historical identities, Quranic attribution or Aramaic validity. Four authors are insufficient to estimate population reliability; same genre does not ensure perfect topic matching.

protocol.reference_predictor: Training-only lexical features and standardization; equal-work author centroids; cosine scoring, as in the attribution benchmark
protocol.interpretation: Descriptive controls; style clusters are not necessarily people. Synthetic damage is not manuscript validation.

grc.interpretation: Catalog-author labels are withheld from features. Multiple clusters within a single author demonstrate why style groups cannot be counted as people.

protocol.reference_predictor: Training-only lexical features and standardization; equal-work author centroids; cosine scoring, as in the attribution benchmark
protocol.interpretation: Descriptive controls; style clusters are not necessarily people. Synthetic damage is not manuscript validation.

hbo.interpretation: Catalog-author labels are withheld from features. Multiple clusters within a single author demonstrate why style groups cannot be counted as people.

grc.interpretation: Synthetic spelling/damage/quotation stress on real text, not actual manuscript/translation invariance. No thresholds tuned on perturbations.

hbo.interpretation: Synthetic spelling/damage/quotation stress on real text, not actual manuscript/translation invariance. No thresholds tuned on perturbations.

grc.interpretation: Held-out editions share a canonical work and are never independent author labels. This limited edition check does not establish invariance across manuscript traditions or translations.

hbo.reason: no independently sourced same-work edition pair

limitations: Observed labels are reference-corpus attributions, not independently proven ancient identities.
Passing measures this deterministic lexical baseline and corpus only; it does not validate AI profiles, clustering, or scripture attribution.

Intervals are conditional descriptive intervals from resampling fixed held-out predictions by work. They do not refit features, scaling, centroids, or calibration; dependencies from shared training works and candidate authors are unmodeled. They are not calibrated uncertainty for unseen corpora or historical attribution.
The predefined function/common-word ablation (machine key closed_class) includes common content verbs in the Greek and Hebrew lists; it is not topic-free.
Authors, periods, editors, and manuscripts may be confounded in the sampled corpus.
At least 8 reference authors and 60 independent works per language/length are required for a pass; small samples remain pilots.
No canonical or disputed scripture is treated as known authorship ground truth.
Open-set rejection uses known-author calibration only; unseen authors may resemble known authors and be falsely accepted.
Topic and genre metadata subsets are descriptive and not equivalent to a fully matched corpus.
A failure is evidence against the tested reliability claim; an inconclusive result is not evidence of reliability.
